what: GEFSv12 reforecast, control member, 3-hourly rain on the 0.25 degree grid (data/gefs/c00) as basin means for the local days t+1, t+2, t+3 of every issue day t, with the AORC rain of the same days beside it (E2, step 2 of ROADMAP.md)

issue_days.what: local calendar days; day t is issued at its local midnight (24:00 by the wall clock of the gauge, summer time included)

rule.run: the 00 UTC run of the UTC date t+1 (init_date = t+1): 4 h old at the Eastern issue time in summer, 5 h in winter, 5 or 6 h at the Central one (the latest 00 UTC run that exists at the issue time; the run of the date t+2 starts after it)
rule.local_day: local day t+k = the wall-clock day of the gauge (zoneinfo America/New_York, America/Chicago for Leaf River, summer time included), forecast hours (lo, hi] of the run with lo = local midnight that starts the day, hi = the one that ends it, counted from the run's start; the amounts of the 3-hourly windows inside the day are summed, a window that straddles a boundary is split in proportion to the time inside (1/3 or 2/3, uniform rain inside a window assumed)
rule.basin_mean: sum over the grid boxes of weight x rain, the weights being the shares of the outline's area in each 0.25 degree box (exact intersections in EPSG:5070)
rule.tables: the first row is 2000-01-01; k = 1, 2, 3 in the column names; mm per local day; fc_raw = the forecast as the model gives it, fc_bc = fc_raw x the bias factor of the basin and lead, aorc = the AORC rain of the same local day t+k

grid.units: the store holds tenths of a mm per 3 h window (data/gefs/README.md); here mm

made_up_values_test.what: every run after the run issued on day c (the runs of the dates c+1 and later) was replaced by random rain (0 to 200 mm per window): the forecasts issued on or before day c did not change (array_equal), and the one issued on c+1 did

subdaily_alignment.what: the basin-mean 3-hourly rain of every window of every run against the AORC rain of the same absolute window moved by s hours (s = -6 .. +6; AORC value stamped T = the hour ending at T), correlation pooled over all runs and the 26 windows, per basin. Asserted: the best shift of the median over the basins is 0 and that of every basin 0 or -1 hour (the curve is flat between -1 and 0: the forecast's rain comes about half an hour earlier than the AORC rain, well inside the forecast model's own timing error): the UTC stamps of the two products and the run times agree to the hour

clock.independent_route: the weights of the windows were computed twice, from forecast hours counted from the run's start and from absolute epoch-second times of the windows and of the day's start and end: identical (largest difference 0.0e+00); the day totals of every basin from both: largest difference < 1e-9 mm

realtime_margin.source: results/data_access.json, gefs_reforecast_record.task5_issue_time.operational_gefs_posting_latency_gec00_0p25: the OPERATIONAL control member on AWS (noaa-gefs-pds), posting time of each forecast-hour file after the run's start, 4 days (2026-10-03 .. 06), the slowest of the four used; the reforecast archive has no posting times and a real-time service would read the operational files

aorc.source: data/aorc (code/fetch_aorc.py), hourly basin means, UTC, the stamp = the end of the hour; summed over the wall-clock day by the code of 16_aorc_rain_to_midnight.py (copied here; its proofs of the day boundaries are run here for 1980-10-01 .. 2014-10-03); the AORC rain of local day t+k is read from the day series by date

bias.rule: bias factor per basin and lead = (sum of the AORC rain of the local days t+k) / (sum of the forecast rain of the same days) over the issue days whose TARGET day t+k lies in the validation years 2000-10-01 .. 2005-09-30 (flood.SPLIT['val']); fc_bc = fc_raw x factor, for every day of 2000-2014 (a factor fitted on the validation years only, applied unchanged to the test years); a single factor per basin and lead: no seasonal correction

skill.how_to_read: the raw forecast against the AORC rain of the same local day; per basin and lead (l1 = day t+1 ...). correlation = Pearson over daily values; mean_ratio = mean forecast / mean AORC; windows: all = target days 2000-01-01 .. 2014-09-30, validation_years = 2000-10-01 .. 2005-09-30 (the years the bias factor is fitted on), test_years = 2005-10-01 .. 2014-09-30; by_season by the month of the target day. Brier: days with at least 5 mm (or 10 mm) of AORC rain, test years, climatology = the sample's own event frequency (BS_clim = f(1-f)); yes_no_* = the control member as a deterministic yes/no forecast (forecast >= threshold), calibrated_probability = a monotone (isotonic) map from the raw forecast amount to the probability of the event, fitted on the validation years with the 12 basins pooled (per lead and threshold) and scored on the test years. A single member is not an ensemble: Guan et al. (2022) quote Brier skill 0.42 (12-36 h) and 0.33 (60-84 h) for the 5 mm days for the probabilities of the whole ensemble; the numbers here are of another kind (one member, a map fitted on the validation years, the sample's own frequency as climatology, these basins and years) and are not a check of that paper

lag_check_correlation_by_shift.how_to_read: correlation of the raw forecast of local day t+k (issue day t) with the AORC rain of local day t+k+shift, shift -2 .. +2, target days 2000-2014

caveats: Control member only (c00, 'low-res ctl'): no ensemble mean, no spread. A single deterministic member is noisier than the 5-member mean and its day totals place the rain to within the forecast's own timing error.

The grid boxes are 0.25 degree (about 25 km, 630 km2) and the basins 113 to 1,928 km2: 1 to 9 boxes overlap a basin (weights recorded in basins.<id>.weights). The forecast is the model's box-mean rain, smoother and drier in its peaks than a basin mean of 1 km rain.

The issue-time margin (realtime_margin): a real-time service would have the run 40 to 100 minutes before the issue time in winter and about 15 minutes too late for the last files (hours after about 39) in Eastern summer; this archive does not check whether the operational control member had the same posting times in 2000-2014, and the 00 UTC run was the only one of the reforecast. The rule 'the run of the UTC date t+1' is kept for every day and basin, as the work order says.

The bias factor is one number per basin and lead fitted on the validation years (mean AORC / mean forecast). The forecast's bias has a season (by_season in the skill record: a wetter control member in spring and summer), which one factor does not remove; a seasonal factor was not used.
AORC is the reference, not the truth: an analysis anchored on gauges and radar (hours before 2002 disaggregated daily totals). The forecast's skill 'against AORC' is skill against that analysis.

Rain amounts of a local day are the sum of 3-hourly windows with straddling windows split in proportion (uniform rain inside a window assumed); for a=4, 5 or 6 the first window of day t+1 is split 1/3-2/3 or 2/3-1/3 or not at all, and the same at the end of each day.
The Brier scores belong to a deterministic forecast (yes/no) or to a calibration of its amount; neither is the probability forecast of an ensemble.
